  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant
to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City
Council Meeting of October 5, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. (Or 1:00 P.M. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other
electronic means, as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance

  Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received will be made
  part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with
  any questions.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  October 5, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
October 5, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item.

Caller (Name Unknown) spoke requesting more information pertaining to Closed Session
Item No. CS-1.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:05 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and
Parking Authority, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ Parking
Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/ Parking Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority officials and personnel
present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager/Acting Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Parking
Authority.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman Butts inquired if
there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/ on any item on the Agendas other than
the public hearings.
   October 5, 2021

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Item No. DR-1, Adoption of a resolution
  required by AB 361 to continue teleconference meetings for the City Council and all City
  Boards and Commissions for the month of October 2021.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. DR-1, Adoption of a
  resolution required by AB 361 to continue teleconference meetings for the City Council
  and all City Boards and Commissions for the month of October 2021, 4, Agreement with
  CEM Construction Corporation for As-Needed Repair Service on Sewer System for the
  City of Inglewood, and CSA-2, Agreement with Miller Barondess, LLP, increasing the
  hourly rates for non-MSG related legal matters, for broad ranging legal advice, guidance,
  and representation.

  PROCLAMATION – DECLARING OCTOBER 21, 2021, AS THE GREAT
  CALIFORNIA SHAKE OUT. Mayor Butts read a proclamation recognizing October
  21, 2021, as The Great California Shake Out.

125  RESOLUTION NO. 22-01 ADOPTED – CONTINUE TELECONFERENCE
  MEETINGS OF THE CITY COUNCIL AND ALL CITY BOARDS AND
  COMMISSIONS FOR THE MONTH OF OCTOBER 2021 AS REQUIRED BY AB
  361. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution making findings required by AB 361 to continue teleconference meetings of
  the City Council and all City Boards and Commissions for the month of October 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that Resolution No. 22-01 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL
  TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCED PUBLIC MEETINGS FOR
  THE CITY COUNCIL AND ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  September 30, 2021, in the amount of $2,898,544.12, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman/
  Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2021-001
  (ZCA -2021-001) TO CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE.
  Mayor Butts or
  public hearing continued to October 12, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 22-002 APPROVED – HELEN LESSICK. Staff report dated
  October 5, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a one-year agreement with
  Helen Lessick (with the option to extend for two additional years in one-year increments)
  for public art consulting services.

  2
   October 5, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 22-002 in an amount not to exceed
  $72,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 22-003 APPROVED – STATE OF CALIFORNIA;
  RESOLUTION NO. 22-02 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-
  2022 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of the attached agreement with the State of California for acceptance of the
  Fiscal Year 2022 Office of Traffic Safety grant funds.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 22-003 in the total amount of
  $245,000; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 22-02 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE ACCEPTANCE
  OF GRANT FUNDS FROM THE OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $245,000

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-004 APPROVED – CEM
  CONSTRUCTION CORPORATION. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was
  presented recommending award of a contract and approval of a two-year agreement with
  CEM Construction Corporation, for As-Needed Repair Service on Sewer System for City
  of Inglewood, per Request for Bid No. RFB-0133.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 22-004 in an
  amount not to exceed $378,675 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency of $34,425).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-005 APPROVED –
  PSOMAS. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was presented recommending award of a
  contract and approval of an agreement with PSOMAS, for the Construction Management
  and Inspection Services for Traffic Signal Safety Improvements for La Brea Avenue
  [HSIPL-5164 (031)] and Prairie Avenue [HSIPL-5164 (032)] Project, per Request for
  Proposal No. RFP-0167.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 22-005 in an
  amount not to exceed $511,660.60 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the
  amount of $46,514.60). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 171  RESOLUTION NO. 22-03 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-
  2022 BUDGET. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was presented recommending the
  adoption of resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Budget to reorganize the
  Library Services Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 22-03 entitled:

  3
   October 5, 2021

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2021-2022 BUDGET TO REORGANIZE THE LBRARY SERVICES
  DEPARTMENT

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – WANDA M. BROWN V. CITY
  OF INGLEWOOD, ET AL.  Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client
  Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding Pending Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Wanda M. Brown v. City of
  Inglewood, et al.; LASC Case No.:21STCV030604.

  No Actions Taken.

125  AMENDMENT NO. 4 TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-118 APPROVED – MILLER
  BARONDESS, LLP. Staff report dated October 5, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of Amendment No. 4 to Agreement No. 18-118 with Miller Barondess, LLP,
  increasing the hourly rates for non-MSG related legal matters, for broad ranging legal
  advice, guidance, and representation.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/ Parking Authority
  Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/
  Parking Authority Member Padilla that the City Council/Successor Agency/ Parking
  Authority does hereby approve Amendment No. 4 to Agreement No. 18-118. The motion
  was moved by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Parking Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman/
  Parking Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, informed residents
  about open drop boxes and their locations for the upcoming November 2, 2021, Election.
  She also stated ballots have been mailed out and shared voting information regarding the
  November 2, 2021, Election.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Ray Howler commented on the Parking & Traffic Commission meeting which was
  attended by 80 residents. During the Parking & Traffic Commission meeting he stated
  residents voiced their concerns regarding the impact of SoFi Stadium and the affect it has
  on the parking permit program. He also requested quantitative data supporting the
  complaints from residents related to the parking permit program.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Police Oversight Commission meetings, and
  requested a meeting with Police Chief Mark Fronterotta. She also mentioned Civil and
  ADA Rights violations.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke in favor of Measures H & I. He also commented on the
  City being in good shape but felt financial management was needed.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:34 p.m.

  Approved this 26th day of October, 2021.

  4
 October 5, 2021

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
